name: Save the Cat! Beat Sheet
description: Blake Snyder's 15-beat structure from 'Save the Cat!' — the most widely used modern screenplay structure.

beats.title: Opening Image
beats.description: A visual that represents the struggle and tone of the story. A 'before' snapshot.

beats.title: Theme Stated
beats.description: Someone (usually not the protagonist) states the movie's theme, often in a casual way. The protagonist doesn't understand it yet.

beats.title: Set-Up
beats.description: Explore the protagonist's status quo life. Show their flaws, their world, and all the things that need fixing. Introduce key supporting characters.

beats.title: Catalyst
beats.description: The moment that changes everything. A life-changing event that knocks the protagonist out of their ordinary world.

beats.title: Debate
beats.description: The protagonist debates: should I go? Is this wise? What if I fail? This is the last chance to turn back.

beats.title: Break into Two
beats.description: The protagonist decides to act and enters Act 2's upside-down world. This must be a proactive choice, not something that happens to them.

beats.title: B Story
beats.description: The subplot begins — often a love story or friendship. This carries the theme of the movie and provides the protagonist with new perspective.

beats.title: Fun and Games
beats.description: The 'promise of the premise.' This is why people bought the ticket — the trailer moments. The protagonist explores the new world and seems to be winning.

beats.title: Midpoint
beats.description: A false victory or false defeat at the story's center. Stakes are raised. The clock starts ticking. The fun is over and consequences become real.

beats.title: Bad Guys Close In
beats.description: External pressures tighten. Internal doubts multiply. The team unravels. The antagonist gains ground. Everything the protagonist built starts to crumble.

beats.title: All Is Lost
beats.description: The opposite of the Midpoint. Everything falls apart. A 'whiff of death' — someone or something dies (literally or metaphorically).

beats.title: Dark Night of the Soul
beats.description: The protagonist wallows in hopelessness. They've lost everything and have no idea how to proceed. They must dig deep to find new strength.

beats.title: Break into Three
beats.description: Eureka! A new idea, fresh inspiration (often from the B Story) gives the protagonist the solution. They synthesize everything they've learned.

beats.title: Finale
beats.description: The protagonist executes their new plan. Old world and new world synthesize. The protagonist proves they've changed by applying the theme. The antagonist is defeated.

beats.title: Final Image
beats.description: The opposite of the Opening Image. Proof that change has occurred. The 'after' snapshot.
